t:
Who would have thought that people and vampires could live in peace anywhere? But, believe it or not, there is such a place! It is called Enoch Isle. Once Enoch was a backwater islet of two villages. And then, not so long ago, vampires who had renounced their creator, Armando de Doucer, arrived on the island. Somehow they came to an agreement with the peasants, and they receive blood in exchange for their goods, healing magic and other useful things. You won't believe it, but I saw with my own eyes that people and vampires live in perfect harmony! But everything changed when werewolves appeared on Enoch. A savage pack of half-intelligent beasts invaded Enoch, and peaceful life came to an end. Their leader, the former bandit chieftain Lyut the Bobtailed, has sworn to devour everyone who does not bow before him. The vampires have shut themselves off from the werewolves with magical barriers, closing the passages between the villages, and together with the peasants they are holding back the monsters' attacks with the last of their strength. So if your adventures take you to Enoch, prepare for a fierce battle! Until you manage to completely clear both villages of werewolves, you will not reach their leader.

Bosses: Murk, Paul de Doucer, Vasilissa the Terrible, Lyut the Bobtailed.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Kanian allod, though vampires of the House de Doucer have settled there alongside the Kanians.

t:
A distant and inaccessible cloister — the dream of every bachelor in Sarnaut. And no wonder, since this allod is inhabited exclusively by maidens, every one of them clever and beautiful. Seekers of romantic adventure should be careful, though. The beauties fled to Fenia's Cloister in search of a calm and quiet life, so they welcome guests very reluctantly.

Bosses: Lagoda Vereskova, Softpaw, Poleaxe the Merciless, Fenia.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian settlement.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Fenia's Island? Ah, that's the old Kanian fortress where those... what do you call them... right, I remember — the feminists! Or femmeists? Anyway, they're women who believe men wrong and oppress them, which has driven them clean out of their minds. No, you tell me — does anyone wrong women in the Empire? It's in the League that folk are completely savage; they even have a saying there, "a hen's no bird, and a woman's no person." Whereas with us she's every bit a person! Only our Imperial ladies run off to that Cloister regularly too... I don't understand why they've turned so against men?! Well, never mind, listen further. Their leader is some Fenia, a mad sorceress who proclaimed herself a goddess incarnate and the patroness of women. She announced that all the evil in the world comes from men, and decided to wage a merciless war on us — on men, that is! And the funniest thing is that some cracked heads actually believed her! Or rather, it was funny right up until they killed every man on the island, and the parts of their bodies — well, the ones that matter most to a man — they... All right, I don't want to talk about it. A friend of mine, Afanasy Nikitov, was there and saw it all with his own eyes. The horrors he told me... He escaped by a miracle! In short, there are no men in the Cloister now. Instead there's a crowd of women of every race, gone feral for lack of male attention and fanatical to the marrow, ready to tear apart any man who ends up on the island. Now there's a paradox — they hate men, yet without men they turn into beasts. No, I'll never understand women. Especially women who reach for a sword at the slightest thing and try to lop off what's most precious. Ahem. I meant the head, actually, not what you were thinking!

Bosses: Lagoda Vereskova, Softpaw, Poleaxe the Merciless, Fenia.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by ogres and elemental spirits.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Ah, Firefrost and its temple... An island where bitter cold and scorching flame exist in peace and harmony. A beautiful place! And everything that looks beautiful in the Astral is in fact deadly dangerous. I advise you to remember that, and to give Firefrost a wide berth. Before, only wild goblins and trolls lived there, but now, they say, the island has also been overrun by elementals. The cause, I suppose, is the recent eruption of a volcano long thought extinct. And they also say that over all of them stands a mysterious spirit, born of the two elements. I'd like to have a look at that marvel! In short, if you're not afraid of elementals and have no wish to live forever, you can find yourself a sturdy crew and give them battle. After all, it is an ancient temple, and countless riches must surely be hidden in it. It would be a sin to let such goods go to waste!

Bosses: Hestia, Bedlam, Blinder, Diamond.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
The Forgotten Temple? And what, may I ask, has drawn your interest to that accursed place? Believe me, anyone who ends up there will want to forget the nightmares they lived through as quickly as possible. Once it was a heap of June ruins of no interest to anyone, in the middle of an islet of no interest even to demons, but then the Wormfaces reached the temple and awoke the flame that had slumbered in it for centuries. The island blazed like a torch until, by a whim of fate, it collided with an icy fragment of another island. Now half of the island on which the temple stands breathes fire, while on the other half you can freeze to the bone. On top of that it is full of aggressive elementals, old but still working sentry golems, and Wormfaces who greatly dislike strangers. Still, there are madmen among the Historians ready to risk their lives for knowledge. I heard that an expedition led by Martin de Blizare recently set out for the Forgotten Temple... And nobody has heard of that expedition since!

Bosses: Glacier, Ekaterina Arhivina, Sleepless Guard, Az and Yaz.

Climate: Temperate and tundra; the allod consists of four shards.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by elemental spirits and the June.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

t:
Far out in the Astral I once happened upon an island where eternal winter reigns. It is ruled by Yaver Arteia, a mad Arisen woman who calls herself the Snow Queen. Oh, what a vile hag she is, I tell you! I escaped from that island by a sheer miracle. The Snow Queen's favorite pastime is to abduct people and set them all manner of riddles. Fail to guess one, and you are turned into an ice statue! In her ice castle Yaver Arteia keeps whole galleries of ice sculptures that were once orcs, gibberlings, Arisen, humans... Her heart is as cold as her icy throne!

That merciless shrew was all set to turn me into an ice statue, and only by a miracle did I get away.

Yaver Arteia must be stopped! If she simply killed people, fine — you'd rest a while in Purgatory, and that's that. But she turns them into statues. Just imagine: a man stands there, unable to move, to breathe, even to close his eyes. And so for a year, two, ten... Brr, how horrible. No, such cold-blooded torment cannot go unpunished!

But reaching the queen will not be easy. Chill, a mad werebear shaman, faithfully guards his mistress's peace. And rumor has it that in especially fierce blizzards a huge bear named Helad appears on the island — though whether that is true, it will be up to you to find out.

Bosses: Helad, Sharptooth, Chill, Yaver Arteia.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited mainly by trolls and lamias.

t:
What do you think of goblins?

On the one hand — pitiful creatures. Everyone laughs at them and despises them a little. They are the heroes of countless jokes and the pets of orc shamans. Sometimes you simply feel sorry for them.

And on the other hand? Thieves and bandits. Mischief-makers, always ready to do something vile. Ever had dealings with the arms mafia on the Coba Plateau? There you go!

There is a goblin island in the Astral. Their stronghold. A Republic! They even elect one of those, what's it called... such a funny word... a president! For three terms in a row now a shaman named Urub has been elected that very president. It is he who organizes the goblins' pirate raids.

If in your wanderings you manage to find that island — carry out the sentence and behead the goblin republic!

Bosses: Goblin Overseer, Buzz, Urub.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a goblin settlement.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

What do you think of goblins? On the one hand, they are unfortunate creatures. Everyone makes fun of them and despises them a little. They are the heroes of countless jokes and the pets of orc shamans. Sometimes you just feel sorry for them. And on the other hand? Thieves and bandits. Nasty pests, always ready to do something low. Ever had dealings with the arms mafia on Coba Plateau? There you go! There is a goblin island in the Astral. Their stronghold. A Republic! They even elect themselves this, what's it called... such a funny word... a president every year! For three terms running a shaman named Urub has been elected that very president. It is he who organizes the goblins' pirate raids. If in the course of your wanderings you manage to find this island — carry out the sentence and behead the goblin republic!

It resembles Siveria.

The island was supposed to be populated entirely by hostile goblins, with no quests and no friendly NPCs.

But it was found without NPCs or monsters... It is mentioned on the astral island Drought (Waters of the Great Canyon).

[Map missing]

Climate: Tundra, closest to the Frozen Frontier archipelago.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, presumably one of the main goblin allods.

Story:

The island was supposed to be populated entirely by hostile goblins, without quests or friendly NPCs. It was found without NPCs or mobs... It is mentioned on the allod of Drought (Waters of the Great Canyon), and also in quests on Coba Plateau and in many other places.

Bosses: no information.

t:
Climate: Tundra. Closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the grave of a June hunter.

Story:

We are met by the Fearless Family of Gibberlings. They told us that they were sent here by an elder from the Frozen Frontier to find some blood artifact that Nordrak needs so badly. It should be somewhere near the grave of the great June dragon hunter Yad-Volk (he imprisoned Nordrak on the Frozen Frontier). Along the way we try to solve the riddle of the grave: on one of the obelisks a wolf is drawn, and next to it two stones with patterns — and it is these we seek out. The first stone drops from the Yeti Leader, the second is carried by the Harpy Chieftainess. We insert these stones into the hollows of the obelisk in the center of the allod. In a snowstorm Yad-Volk and a Ghostly Dragon appear. After the victory over the dragon, we take the blood artifact from the stele and give it to the Gibberlings.

Bosses: Polar Yeti Leader, Rock Harpy Chieftainess, Ghostly Dragon.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into the Whirl.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
It resembles Asee-Teph.

We meet an unknown Elf, who introduces himself as a hero with many feats to his name (he is lying shamelessly), sent by the Conclave of Great Mages to obtain dragon blood. He proposes that we team up and, before setting out on the job, asks us to practise on a draconid. We make our way to the cave with the dragon and kill it. The Elf thanks us for the help and shows off, saying that one day we too will become as famous as he is.

[Map missing]

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph and the Dragon Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by draconids.

Story:

On the island we meet a mysterious individual who tells us about his supposed exploits and says that his task is to obtain the blood of the Great Dragon. He asks us to get some practice before we go after the Great Dragon together with him, and to clear the island of draconids, killing their leader in the process. When we return victorious, the Mysterious Individual says that while we were resting and amusing ourselves with the draconids, he found out that the Great Dragon is in a cave on the other end of the island, and it is time to finish him off. After the victory, the Mysterious Individual says that we did well to defeat the Dragon, and that he, too, started out with exploits just like these and is now a great hero. In a word, showing off.

Bosses: Draconid Boss, Dragon (great).

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Oh, I wouldn't advise you to get mixed up with the draconids. Dangerous creatures. Even the demon hunters who have made an alliance with them do not fully trust these beings. And why? Because the draconids guard their secrets like the apple of their eye! And they do not trust them even to their friends.

I do not know what secret is kept in the Green Maze. The Historians who tried to explore it never managed to get into its far part, access to which is closed off by a magical barrier. As soon as they tried to get past it, two supreme draconids appeared — two Guardians of the Limit, as they call themselves — and drove the Historians out. Since then the draconids greet all uninvited guests with steel.

If risk is to your taste, you can try to uncover the secret of the Green Maze. But you will have to find your own way through the ancient ruins.

Bosses: Version 1: Supreme Spellcaster, Supreme Healer, Cursed Warrior. Version 2: Supreme Spellcaster, Supreme Healer, Reborn Warrior, Twice Born.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Draconids.

Story:

t:
Have you ever heard of Volcano Isle? No? Then listen. Not long ago a tribe of draconids appeared on this island, worshipping a fire god who sleeps in the crater of a long-extinct volcano. With constant sacrifices the draconids kept him asleep, so that he would not awaken and his scorching fury would not break loose. But not long ago their high priest broke with custom and summoned the sleeper. The volcano awoke, and a mighty fire elemental burst out. From tongues of flame and the heat of flowing magma he created four guardians — huge fiery manticores whose breath can burn anyone to ashes on the spot! If you decide to go to the island and try to awaken the sleeping flame, you must repeat the draconids' ritual, laying the fiery hearts of shellbacks on the sacrificial altars. But don't even try to take him on while his faithful manticores are alive! The fire god put a particle of his power into each guardian, and with their deaths he will be greatly weakened. That's all I know about Volcano Isle. Good luck to you!

Bosses: Supreme Draconid, Bonesnapper, Hephaesto.

Climate: Tropical. Closest to the Kingdom of Elements.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by fire elementals and draconids.

t:
And how do you know about that, eh?

That's classified information! The Committee will wring your neck for divulging it!

Oh, all right. Since you already know about the heretics themselves, so be it — I'll share it with you in secret. But mind you, not a word to anyone!

The Heretic Refuge is a stain on the reputation of all the Arisen. After all, it is from their people that all these dangerous madmen come!

The heretics refuse to recognize the holiness of Nezeb, Tensess and Skrakan. They believe that all that exists arose from four elements — fire, earth, water, and nature as the union of all three pure elements. And they have grown so hidebound in their heresy that they accept no arguments of reason. They fiercely hate everyone who does not share their faith. After several high-profile murders committed by this sect, the Church, with the full support of the Committee and of Yasker himself, anathematized them and opened a hunt for them.

The heretics — or rather, the handful that was left of their sect — seized an astral ship in port and vanished into the depths of the Astral. Time passed, and their existence was simply forgotten; all the documents were classified and handed over to the archive. And not long ago a captain I know told me he had heard about the heretics from someone who had seen with his own eyes a man who had the misfortune to stumble upon their refuge in the Astral. That poor wretch barely escaped! His ship was scorched by fire, a gaping hole from a huge boulder yawned in the hold, all the rigging was covered in mold, and half the crew had turned into ice statues...

So if your adventures lead you to the secret refuge of the heretics, know this — they are mad killers, and they will try to destroy you at any cost!

Bosses: Yasskul Flach, Negus Minhotep, Negus Haifa, Negus Zirach.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Zem fanatics and heretics.

t:
I've never had occasion to visit the Edge island.

It got its name because it often appears near the Holy Land. No wonder the League and the Empire sought to seize it to use as an additional base. Our side proved quicker.

But now access to the island is forbidden. The Xadaganian garrison defending the Edge has betrayed the Empire! Evidently there were demon cultists among them who managed to cloud the soldiers' minds. Or perhaps the whole thing is down to the astral worm that has dug in in the middle of the island. They say it can have a destructive effect on the mind.

Elizaveta Rysina herself recently summoned me and questioned me about the heroes of the Empire. The thing is, our side currently has no way to send a punitive expedition to the island. And yet the traitors must be punished! And the island cleansed of demons!

Bosses: Cultist Captain, Garm, Astral Worm.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land island), and also to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, the site of a research base.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Bosses: Cultist Captain, Garm, Astral Worm.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
If you open a primer at the letter "K" (for krepost, "fortress"), you can see a fortress surrounded by a sturdy stone wall. That picture appeared long, long ago, and as his model the artist used the Hunters' Stockade — an exemplary defensive structure of those times. It was built before the Cataclysm, when the Abatis Line was being laid — a long chain of fortifications against orc raids.

After the catastrophe the fortress vanished into the Astral along with other shards of the old world.

Bosses: Blitzkrieg, Zugunder, Paunch, Kaput.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land island), and also to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the site of a demon hunters' base.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

It's an ancient fortress, a venerable one. His-to-ri-cal! The Kanians built it even before the Cataclysm, when they were laying the Abatis Line — a long chain of fortifications against orc raids. How many times it was besieged, how many times burnt to the ground — and every time it was rebuilt. So it stood right up until the catastrophe, and then, together with other shards of the old world, it was lost in the Astral. And now, centuries later, the Demon Hunters found it — dilapidated, but all in one piece. Some say it was the courage of many generations of defenders that preserved it, others insist on an astral anomaly... Be that as it may, the Hunters rebuilt it, reinforced it with meteorite shards and turned it into one of their most powerful strongholds. Demons are afraid to sail within cannon shot of it!

Bosses: Blitzkrieg, Zugunder, Paunch, Kaput.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
A strange little place... Maybe that island truly exists, maybe it's a mirage, a phantasm, a glamour. The island is covered in thick forests and deep bogs. All sorts of creatures live there, some intelligent, some you couldn't really call that. I saw kikimoras, satyrs, I even saw a talking fox! And above all — there are hordes of ghosts there! Kanians mostly, sort of alive and sort of not. And they all obey the mistress of the place — Ziva, I think she's called — whether she's a woman, a bird, or some kind of spirit altogether. A peaceful place; the mistress was kind to us that time, gave us rest and shelter. Only I've heard from other travelers that some misfortune befell it recently — an unhappy love, or some curse... In short, I'd think twice before mooring at Iriy without holy water and loaded cannons.

Bosses: Bosk, Mister and Missus, Naiad, Marena.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by forest creatures and nature spirits.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

A strange little place... Either that island really exists, or it is a mirage, a phantom, a delusion. That island is covered with dense forests and deep swamps. All sorts of creatures live there, some sentient and some not so much. I saw kikimoras, satyrs, I even saw a talking fox! And most importantly — there are ghosts there without number! Mostly Kanians, seemingly alive and yet not. And they all obey the mistress of that place, Ziva is her name, I think — whether a human, or a bird, or some kind of spirit altogether. A peaceful little place; the mistress was welcoming to us that time, gave us rest and shelter. Only I heard from other travellers that some misfortune happened there recently — whether an unhappy love or some curse... In short, I would think twice about putting in at Iriy without holy water and loaded cannons!

Bosses: Bosk, Mister and Missus, Naiad, Marena.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Long ago honest folk jokingly called one distant district the Far-Far-Away Kingdom. It was a real backwater: a rider couldn't get through, nor a man on foot. A wall of trees — for hundreds of versts! And this land was ruled by a wise guardian — the living soul of the forest. She did not favor wicked travelers, but for good ones the path through the thicket unrolled of its own accord.

After the Cataclysm only a pitiful scrap of that forest remained. And the guardian, they say, survived — she watches over her domain as in the old days. Every traveler can count on shelter and rest under the canopy of the ancient trees. But Light forbid anyone should harm the local animals! It is said more than one poachers' vessel has vanished without a trace near the Isle of Far-Far-Away!

Bosses: Forest Spirit, Veleslav Dubov, Blackmarin, Forest Guardian.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by forest fauna and spirits.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Isle of Far-Far-Away? Hm... As an acquaintance of mine put it: "Calm, smooth, and the grace of Tensess." And where does such a strange name come from? Well, it's a funny story. Long ago, before the Cataclysm, one remote Kanian province had a name so jaw-breaking that it wasn't preserved even in official charters. And the inhabitants themselves jokingly called their land the Kingdom of Far-Far-Away. It was a real backwater... Forest, forest and nothing but forest! Thousands of hectares of solid green. And it was ruled by a guardian — the living soul of the forest. They say whoever entered that forest with ill thoughts never came out again. Well, after the Cataclysm only a pitiful scrap of that forest remained. But it held out and did not melt away in the astral. And the guardian, they say, survived too. Knowledgeable people told me that her magic still protects the island. Every traveler can count on shelter and rest under the canopy of the age-old trees. But Light forbid you anger the mistress of the forest! If you try to turn the local animals into shashlik, you won't have time to blink before you're turned into cutlets yourself.

Bosses: Forest Spirit, Veleslav Dubov, Blackmarin, Forest Guardian.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Do you know the story of the Isle of the Damned? No? It's a story about how the Darkness in the soul is more terrible than the Darkness outside.

On a distant island lost in the Astral there was a small village. Good people lived there, honest and hard-working. And among them were two young lovers, Ivan and Marya. When the time came, they were wed, all properly and decently, and began to live happily and prosper. That's where the fairy tale should end... Only you and I don't live in a fairy tale.

There was a man in that village, an outsider. A bad, envious man. He couldn't calmly watch the newlyweds' happiness and Marya's beauty — he was terribly jealous of Ivan.

And he decided to destroy the young couple. By deceit he got hold of Marya's wedding ring, a love letter and the bride's bouquet, which had stayed unwithered ever since the wedding, and with the help of these things he laid a terrible curse on the young couple.

Because of that curse both young people soon went to their graves. Only the evil did not go unpunished: the curse fell upon the whole island, and the villain himself was not spared by it. He died and turned into vicious undead.

And the souls of the young couple remained restless. There is no bright path for them while the curse lies upon them. To lift it, you will first have to find the ring, the letter and the flowers the villain used for the curse, bring them to the young couple's grave, and then set the souls free.

Bosses: Heartbreaker, Shishimora, Korosten, Ivan Neladov and Maria Neladova.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the site of a Kanian hamlet.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Do you know the story of the Isle of the Damned? No? Well, it's not the kind of story you tell children at bedtime... A sad story, a bad one. A story about how the darkness in the soul is more terrible than the Darkness outside. On a distant island lost in the Astral there was a small village. Good people lived there, honest, hard-working. And among them were two young lovers, Ivan and Maria. They loved each other ever so dearly. When the time came they were wed, all proper and fitting, and began to live happily and prosper. That would be the end of the fairy tale... Only you and I don't live in a fairy tale. There was a certain man in that village, an outsider. A bad man, an envious one. He could not look calmly upon the newlyweds' happiness, upon Maria's beauty — and she was a lovely girl, the picture of health. He was terribly jealous of Ivan. Before the young couple were wed he kept making advances to Maria, and each time was sent packing, and a couple of times got a punch in the face from Ivan. And once they were married, he lost his mind altogether from black envy. He decided to destroy the young couple. By deceit he obtained Maria's wedding ring, the love letter Ivan had sent her before the wedding, and the bride's bouquet, which had stood unwithered after the wedding, and with the help of these things he laid a terrible curse on the young couple. From that curse both of them soon went to their graves. And so they were buried together. But the evil did not go unpunished — the curse fell upon the whole island, and the villain himself was not spared. He died and turned into vicious undead, and his cronies and accomplices became skeletons. The restless souls of the young couple remained in the grave, and there is no bright path for them while the curse lies upon them. I beg you — free the innocent souls, lift the curse! To do so you will first need to find the ring, the letter and the flowers the villain used for the curse and bring them to the young couple's grave, and then set their restless souls free. Well, will you take on this good deed?

Bosses: Heartbreaker, Shishimora, Korosten, Ivan Neladov and Maria Neladova.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Contested island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into an Astral Dominion island.

t:
Since time immemorial mortals have challenged the Gods. Some daredevils really do manage to succeed and win fame for the ages. But most meet an inglorious end, or even something worse. Nihaz, for instance, created a whole astral island — the Jail. There go the Sparks of those who dared to get under the Lord's divine feet.

The prison allod is guarded without breaks or days off by guards armed to the teeth. The island is considered secret, so visitors are not especially welcome.

Bosses: Bloody Executioner, Farakh, the Overlord's Punishment, Provost.

Climate: Wasteland, closest to the Cradle.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the Overlord's servants.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know about this island only from scraps of information that fell into the hands of Imperial intelligence. In short, it went like this. In one of the sectors an Imperial reconnaissance ship discovered an island not marked on the maps. The captain made several ferrotypes of the island and sent them as an urgent message to the capital. The message said that the captain had decided to carry out reconnaissance. They have not made contact since. You see, this island, which was given the name the Jail, is the prison of the Overlord himself! The ferrotypes show exhausted prisoners locked inside energy domes, and all the passages are blocked by force fields. The territory is patrolled by the Overlord's close servants and battle machines. What's more, there are creatures there that the Committee's experts have identified as high-ranking Wormfaces. According to their theory, it is they who are running what goes on in the Jail at the moment. Which, you'll agree, is somewhat strange — after all, the Wormfaces betrayed the Overlord. From this I can draw one certain conclusion and two guesses. The conclusion: the island is the Overlord's prison, where his servants keep undesirable adventurers. The guesses are these. First, the Wormfaces have somehow managed to subjugate the Overlord's servants. Second, they are hiding from everyone, and we will most likely never see the crew that landed on the shore again. I wouldn't advise you to go there without the support of at least one battleship, or better two. Some mysteries are better never solved...

Bosses: Bloody Executioner, Farakh, the Overlord's Punishment, Provost.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t: Oh, Boyar Jeer is a living legend! Though "living" depends on how you look at it... He is a necromancer, one of the best in the world. Some even say he is a Great one! Whether that's the truth or idle talk, I don't know: for many years now he has lived alone on his estate, talking only with the dead. His peasants are another matter: cheerful, talkative, and not poor either — if the goods are good, they always have a coin to spare. Though a merchant I know was there recently and told me something strange. He steps off the ship, lays out his wares, and the peasants don't so much as glance his way: they all stand stock-still, staring at one point. He looked closer and saw what seemed like a ghostly mist hanging over them all... He took to his heels right away! Whether it's true or not, I don't know — I sell it as I bought it! If you happen to be there — maybe you'll find out the truth?

If you go there, maybe you'll find out the truth?

Bosses: Clockwork Madman, Ill-Rot, Raven Tome, Vasilissa Artful.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian estate.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Oh, Boyar Jeer is a living legend! Though "living" — that depends on how you look at it... He is a necromancer, one of the best in the world. They even say he is a Great Mage! Whether they tell the truth or lie, I do not know: for many years he has lived alone on his estate, talking only to the dead. His peasants are another matter: merry, talkative, and not poor either — if the goods are good, they always have money. True, a merchant I know was there recently and told a strange thing. He comes off his ship, he says, lays out his goods, and the peasants don't even look his way: they all stand stock-still, staring at one point. He looked closer and saw that a ghostly mist seemed to spread over all of them... He took to his heels from there! Whether it's true or not, I do not know — I sell it as I bought it! If you are there — maybe you will find out the truth?

Story allod:

Catherina sent the heroes to Jeer to learn the skill of speaking with the dead. The problem was that Jeer took no apprentices. So a special approach had to be found. The heroes went to him and left empty-handed — Jeer defeated them and threw them into his dungeon. Only with the help of the Bogatyr whom Catherina had sent with them did they manage to break their chains and leave the prison. And on the way they freed another sorceress — Vasilissa Artful, who also thirsted for forbidden knowledge. The freed Vasilissa had a plan for making Jeer take apprentices after all. For that his death had to be found, and Jeer had hidden his death in a needle. He put the needle in a drake, the drake in a hare, and the hare in a chest, which he hung on a black oak. It was not easy to find Jeer's death, but they did manage to obtain it. And the old man had no choice but to agree to teach the heroes the language of the dead. And the needle in which his death was sealed stayed with Vasilissa.

Bosses: Clockwork Madman, Ill-Rot, Raven Tome, Vasilissa Artful.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

t:
The unusual name of this allod, Mboa-Mboa, can most likely be pronounced only by the intelligent lizards who inhabit the island. And although the place is heavenly beautiful, seasoned astral explorers try to steer clear of it. Some travellers say that somewhere in the jungles of Mboa-Mboa lives a huge monster that hurls boulders at astral ships sailing past the island. Most likely these are just tall tales. But of smaller creatures, no less dangerous, the allod has plenty: predatory turtles, lions and even crocodiles.

Bosses: Swiss, Zuul, Boomer, Tom-Tom.

Climate: Tropical, closest to the Pearl Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Draconids.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know little about the jungles of Mboa-Mboa. Once we went far, far away, into the very deepest layers of the Astral. We were already thinking of turning back when land appeared on the horizon. We came closer and gasped — what beauty! Everything green, blooming, fragrant, butterflies of every colour of the rainbow flying about, monkeys jumping from palm to palm... Not an island — paradise! Well, that is what we thought until we went ashore. And there... mercy me! I had not seen such hungry creatures in a long time! Huge snakes, bloodsucking mosquitoes, crocodiles with jaws like a trap. So we ran back to the ship, and ran straight into the local aborigines — and next to them the crocodiles seemed a trifle. The scoundrels almost cut us to ribbons. Little, but vicious! After that it only got worse — we escaped the forest folk and ran into Draconids. They gladly invited us to dinner, with us in the role of first course, second course and dessert, so we ran back twice as fast! In short, I will never set foot in those jungles again. To the demons with such cruises!

Bosses: Swiss, Zuul, Boomer, Tom-Tom.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

Gallery: no information.

t:
Frost and cold — that's all I can say about Kyoltmark. I've never been there myself, but I know that one of the first gibberling ships was wrecked on that icy rock. When, a few years later, League ships finally found the rock, the surviving gibberlings had already settled on that miserable scrap of land, made themselves at home and flatly refused to leave the island that had become their home.

But not long ago disaster struck — astral demons attacked the island. And strangest of all, they didn't slaughter the inhabitants but took them captive. They say a mighty demon named the Thought Catcher turned all the gibberlings into his slaves, and now they serve him loyally and devotedly. A terrible fate!

If you find yourself on that island, you won't be able to avoid fighting the maddened gibberlings. Strike without pity — only empty shells remain of the locals, and the demons control their will!

Bosses: Fiend, Guur'Maan, Sharpclaw, Thought Catcher.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a former gibberling settlement (captured by demons).

t:
Climate: Desert, closest to the Catacombs.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by lizards.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Surely you're not planning to join the Historians? Any Historian would give his right hand without a second thought to explore Koch-Itzmahl. Just imagine — a fully preserved temple from the heyday of the June empire. Not those pitiful ruins scattered everywhere, but a complete temple complex. I confess I only glimpsed it, and even then I nearly fell overboard in surprise! Bas-reliefs, frescoes, statues, carved columns... Ah, and how many secrets it hides, how many treasures... But there is no way to get to them! Lizards have overrun the whole island. When we tried to put ashore, they pelted us with spears, burned a huge hole in the sail with a fireball, and kept promising to tear out our hearts and lay them on the altar of their ancestors. Their chief, Shisskh, raged most of all. Ooh, vicious creatures! We had to turn round urgently and move on empty-handed. Clearing the temple of the lizards' presence is a good deed and pleasing to the Light... and a profitable one besides!

Bosses: Caiman, Lion, Bloodberry, Shisskh the Seven-Fingered.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Confrontation island.

Addendum: Over time reworked into an Island of the Astral Dominion.

t: As you can see, the map changed a little, but even so this is one of the most authentic islands. The quests there went like this: we arrive, there are zombies everywhere, we meet a lone survivor… In essence, the story there later stayed the same, only without that soldier. On top of that, a monument to a stone was added as an Easter egg. However, this whole business with the numbered Imperial islands spawned an entire chain of stories about various Zem rising up in the Empire's secret research camps and getting up to no good. Then came White 17, then Zone 51 — roughly about the same thing.

I suppose you already know that many achievements of imperial magic and science owe their existence to closed secret laboratories?

However, there is a dark stain in the chronicle of these glorious deeds. I'm talking about Lab Nine.

Yasskul Setnakhte, a cultist of Tep who knew his master's work firsthand, disrupted the course of important experiments and recreated a terrible disease — the Plague that wiped out the Zem people.

Now the victims of this disease rule the island unchallenged. There is no way to cure them. Only one thing remains — to grant peace both to them and to the head of Lab Nine, General Zubin, who is now called nothing but "General Plague." The infected zombies that carry the disease must also be destroyed. And of course Yasskul Setnakhte himself — the cause of all the plague island's woes — deserves to die. Are you up to this feat?

Bosses: General Plague, Stonecutter, Yasskul Setnakhte.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land), and also the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; a research base is located here.

Story:

We are met by a crowd of vicious undead and the only living man, Iov Milin. He reports to us that this laboratory was engaged in research into necromagic and Tep's technologies. The laboratory was headed by Yasskul Setnakhte, a Zem scientist. However, according to Iov, Yaver was not in his right mind and performed strange experiments on the personnel. Iov reported this to General Zubin, but he wouldn't listen. Our task is to reach Mark Grobin, the commissar, and use a secret artifact to inform the Committee of what has happened. After the communication session, the Committee sends reinforcements here (most likely a cleanup squad), and we are ordered to kill Yasskul Setnakhte. After the victory we get his diary, from which we learn that he was trying to synthesize Tep's plague, and that he succeeded. He himself survived, since he had already lived through Tep's plague, as did one of the soldiers — Iov Milin. Gover's last entry shows that he intended to capture Milin and study him most thoroughly, in order to understand the cause of his resistance to the Plague.

Bosses: General Plague, Yasskul Setnakhte.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Contested island.

Addendum: Over time the island was remade, partly changing the story. It was also reworked into an Isle of the Astral Dominion.

t:
Oh, that is a very interesting place. And a dangerous one!

The Land of a Thousand Wings is a jumble of rocks and fragments of ancient buildings destroyed centuries ago. Three islands are joined together by narrow walkways that offer a dizzying view. And the Land of a Thousand Wings is inhabited by the only ones who can live there without the constant risk of falling into the astral or breaking their necks on the mountain slopes. I mean the Aviaks and the harpies.

As far as I understood, the Aviaks came to the Land of a Thousand Wings first, and the harpies invaded the island much later, and it all ended in a great brawl. But somehow Cual the Stormbearer, the elder of the Aviaks, managed to tame the unruly harpies. He and the harpy queen made peace, and now these two peoples live in complete harmony, helping each other in every way. I even suspect that between Cual himself and Olivia the Temptress there is something more than a business relationship. But that is beside the point.

When I was a guest on this island, I was always struck by Cual's wisdom and quick mind. He even managed to tame a wild manticore that lived in the ruins of the old temple! But in recent years the Aviaks have shut themselves off from the rest of the world, accused both the League and the Empire of greed and stupidity, and deal harshly with anyone who dares to set foot on their land. I do not know what caused this sudden hatred of the other peoples. Perhaps you will manage to find out the reason? But if you really intend to go to the Land of a Thousand Wings — prepare for a fierce battle!

Bosses: Olivia the Temptress, Silverwing, Murka, Cual the Stormbearer.

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Frontier.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by aviaks and harpies.

t:
It resembles Lightwood.

We meet a Sailor who asks for help and sends us to the Great Mage Svetalan. He tells us that the island broke away from Kania long, long ago; it is not large — just a Fortress on a mountain and a small settlement in the valley. But now this settlement has been attacked by strange astral creatures, and the situation must be looked into. In the settlement we find the Voivode, who tells us that they can manage to kill the creatures themselves, one at a time, but a couple of lads who went scouting towards the mill may not survive. The scouts say they saw some cultists, but they are badly wounded and cannot stand against them, so we go to find out their plans and "act according to the situation". In the end, according to the situation, we staged a massacre and set off to Svetalan to tell him what was going on. The chief demon, whom the cultists had managed to summon, invaded the fortress, and the Great Mage asks us to help one last time and destroy it. After the demons are defeated, Svetalan offers to let us stay and to introduce us to his granddaughter (if she survived).

[Map missing]

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a settlement with a fortress.

Story:

The allod was part of Kania (most likely located near the Kanian Archipelago). We are met by a Seasoned Sailor; seeing our astral ship, he asks for help and directs us to the Great Mage of this allod. Svetalan, the Great Mage, tells us that the allod was attacked by astral creatures (demons); part of the retinue went off to defend the settlement, but there is still no news of them. And we are asked to find the survivors and help them cope with the scourge. We fought our way to the voivode; he told us that a hundred or so soldiers went to scout at the mill, and while the voivode and the survivors gather their strength, we go scouting. We defeat a Demon Scout and find the scouts hiding in the mill. They say they noticed some people in hoods on the other bank — apparently cultist conspirators. We kill the cultists and their leader. We return to Svetalan to tell him what happened, but the demons have already got into the town. We must fight our way to the chief demon and defeat him. After the victory over the boss, the Great Mage says that as a sign of gratitude we may stay with them on the allod, and also that, if his granddaughter survived, he will introduce her to us.

Bosses: Ferocious Demon Scout, Master Cultist, Demon Boss.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
I had a friend — Roman Kuzin. A traveler, an explorer. And ill luck carried him to the Lost Isle. There's been no word from him since...

The Lost Isle is a legend. The legend of Tep's Pyramid, which acquired a mind of its own and stamps out undead, placing Sparks into dead bodies. It is known that whoever manages to defeat the Pyramid will get a treasure.

That is exactly what Romka dreamed of. He gathered information about the island. I'll tell it to you if you undertake to find this island and rescue my comrade.

On the Lost Isle you will meet magical elementals that embody the Pyramid's power. You will meet many undead it has created. By destroying them you will be able to reach the Pyramid itself, where you must find a way to shut it down. And if you do that and the Pyramid stops working, its treasure will be your reward.

Well? Will you take on the job?

Bosses: ver. 1: Pulsating Magic Elemental, Cobweb Spider, Pyramid Guardian.

ver. 2: Pulsating Magic Elemental, Cobweb Spider, Zinoviy Semetry, Pyramid Guardian.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, elementals, undead.

t: For as long as I've been ploughing the Astral, this islet was always just a frozen lump of rock — no life, no vegetation. And recently it changed as if by magic: now streams flow there, trees blossom, and there are even some little houses! I put in to shore, and more wonders — creatures live there such as I've never seen in my life. Like Gibberlings, but not Gibberlings, fluffy and long-eared. They are friendly and hospitable, only somehow skittish. They say another tribe lives beyond the mountains, and they are afraid their kin might go to war against them. I wished them the help of the Light, and they gave me a strange look and sent me on my way. A riddle, not an island, honestly!

For as long as I've been sailing the Astral, this little island was always just a frozen rock — no life, no vegetation. But recently it was transformed as if by magic — now there are streams flowing and trees blooming, and even some little houses standing there! I moored at the shore, and more wonders — creatures live there such as I've never seen in my life. Like gibberlings, but not gibberlings, fluffy and big-eared. They're friendly and hospitable, only somehow skittish. They say another tribe lives beyond the mountains, and they fear their kin might make war on them. I wished them the Light's help, and they gave me a strange look and sent me on my way. A riddle, not an island, honest to goodness!

Bosses: Li-Ter, Plamennik, Fluffy, Claire Brightley.

Climate: Taiga, closest to Siveria.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited mainly by Tekyans.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

For as long as I've been ploughing the Astral, that little island was always just a frozen lump of rock — no life, no vegetation. And then recently it was transformed as if by magic: now streams run there, trees bloom, there are even some little houses standing! I put in to shore, and more wonders: creatures live there such as I've never seen in my life. Something like gibberlings, but not gibberlings — fluffy and big-eared. They are friendly and hospitable, only somehow skittish. They say another tribe lives beyond the mountains, and they fear their kin may come to make war on them. I wished them the help of the Light, but they gave me a strange look and sent me on my way. That island is a riddle, upon my word!

Story allod:

Catherina sent the heroes to discover the source of a great power near Umoir, and gave them a Knight to help — the warrior Claire Brightley. Arriving on Lumix Isle (as the island where that sorcery was being worked was called), they witnessed yet another miracle: instead of bare rock and ice, a settlement had appeared on the allod. And not just any settlement, but a village of the Tekyans, who had all perished — destroyed by Tep — and until then had existed only in the Illusory World. Yet these Tekyans were real creatures of flesh and blood. They remembered everything that had happened to them in Tequatl on Irdrich, but how they had come to be on Lumix Isle they did not really understand themselves. They wished to summon their patron Genlun, and to that end had built a statue of him. And Genlun did indeed answer the call, which, however, roused the wrath of Claire, who, being a Paladin, did not wish to have any dealings with a pagan god. Genlun related that a few days earlier something like a shining palm had taken them from Tequatl together with their houses and moved them here, while at the same time trying to erase all memory of their crocodile patron. Genlun sensed that there was another Tekyan village on the island whose people had already stopped believing in him, and he suggested going there. When the heroes and Claire reached the second village, it turned out that the Tekyans living there now worshipped the Light. But their faith was far from kind: to prove that the heroes were not pagans, these Tekyans proposed that they die and be resurrected. Not even Brightley agreed to that, so they had to pacify the fluffy zealots. Further on, the path through the village led them to June ruins, where the captive Klavdia awaited them. She revealed that it was her handiwork — both Lumix Isle and the Tekyans, whom she had managed to bring into the real world with the power of Tep's Spark. And the one who had taken her captive was none other than the Servant of Light himself, the fire-haired angel from Purgatory. Now the heroes and Claire had to fight him as well. What lay behind his displeasure, no one could yet say. But Claire decided to stay on Lumix Isle to keep an eye on Genlun and on the Light-worshipping Tekyans.

Bosses: Li-Ter, Plamennik, Fluffy, Claire Brightley.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

t:
"No minerals. No water. No vegetation. Inhabited by mechanoids" — in most ship's logs this island has not earned a more detailed description. They say that while the cultists and mechanoids of Irdrich were fighting the combined army of the League and the Empire, a rusty barge with Tep's former slaves quietly slipped away from the shore. Evidently the old lord no longer met the fugitives' quality requirements.

But the habit of obedience stayed with the mechanoids, and demand always creates supply. They chose an inconspicuous corner of the Astral and set about building an artificial intelligence — their new deity. Such a project requires an enormous amount of resources, which is why the islet is melting away before your eyes. Ship captains should be careful — after all, astral vessels are an excellent source of valuable materials and equipment.

Bosses: Fill-o-Matic, Nomarkh Megavolt, Negus Augment, Integral.

Climate: Desert, closest to Kirah.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by cultists.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

You probably know what happened on Irdrich. Tep, an ancient necromancer of the Zem people, fancied himself a god and prepared a whole army of mechanoids to enslave all of Sarnaut. In the face of such danger our troops joined forces with the Leaguers and crushed the viper after all. But though Tep is dead, his cause lives on. Every now and then heroes stumble upon lairs of cultists who don't know about the death of their god or refuse to believe in it. And sometimes it's the other way round: some of Tep's slaves turned away from their master. One soldier told me that while the cultists and mechanoids were hacking away at the united army, a rusty barge quietly pulled away from the shore and sailed off in an unknown direction. Maybe it's just a tall tale: I sell it for what I bought it. But if you come across an island of rusty renegades somewhere in the depths of the astral, don't be surprised.

Bosses: Fill-o-Matic, Nomarkh Megavolt, Negus Augment, Integral.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.
